guarantees.claim: error_o is continuously assigned to err, so it reflects the current state of err at all times.
The PRIM_FLOP_SPARSE_FSM macro instance (u_state_regs) latches the state register st to the value of st_gated_d on clock edges, with an idle reset value of StIdle.
st_gated_d is assigned to st (current state) when block_swcmd is asserted; otherwise it is assigned to st_d (next state).

assumptions.claim: The state encoding width ($bits(st)) must equal the parameter StateWidth, and the software command input (sw_cmd_i) must be exactly 6 bits wide.
assumptions.risk: If violated, the error response info field for err_swsequence will be incorrectly sized or misaligned.

assumptions.claim: The configuration mode input (cfg_mode_i) must be exactly 2 bits, and strength input (cfg_strength_i) must be exactly 3 bits.
assumptions.risk: If violated, the error info field for err_modestrength will be mis-sized.

uncertain_points.claim: The clock-gating signal block_swcmd is used in a continuous assignment to hold st_gated_d, but an ICEBOX comment (#14631) indicates a desire to move this condition into an explicit always_ff block to clarify clock gating intent. The sparse encoding macro prevents this, potentially obscuring the gating condition.
uncertain_points.risk: Unclear clock gating documentation may lead to synthesis surprises or lint false positives, but no functional bug is indicated here.
